title: Workspace snapshot retention is age-based with no count/byte budget — ~100 GB steady state at multi-agent commit rate
wanted_capability: A bounded retention policy for materialized workspace snapshots. Every commit materializes a new head-<sha> snapshot (up to 1.6 GB each for d723917f); retention is max_snapshot_age_days (default 14) plus small per-repo/per-workspace recent floors, with no count or byte budget. At this repo's commit rate (~16 snapshots/day across agents) the steady state is ~100 GB even WITH daily GC running — and the daily-compaction-arc's StorageGc node doesn't pass max_snapshot_age_days at all, so it inherits the 14-day default. Wanted: (a) count-cap and/or byte-budget retention per workspace (e.g. keep N newest + total bytes ceiling), (b) the arc's StorageGc args tightened accordingly, (c) consider not materializing a full snapshot per commit (delta or ref-count against the previous head) since consecutive snapshots are near-identical.
fallback_used: Manual bbox_storage_gc with max_snapshot_age_days=0 (90.7 GB / 209 files reclaimed; 25-file recent floor retained).
resolution_note: Budget-bounded retention shipped (worktree storage-maintenance-leaks, commit 883d6ad9): SnapshotRetentionPolicy gains max_count_per_workspace (default 32) + max_total_bytes_per_workspace (default 16 GiB); decisions move to snapshot-dir grain, walked newest-first per workspace; floors (recent workspace/repo, grace) always retain and consume budget; age keep applies only within budget. bbox_storage_gc exposes both as params; the in-daemon 6h pass inherits budgets via GcPolicy::default(); daily-compaction-arc v2 passes max_snapshot_age_days=7 + both budgets and is installed on prod (old binary honors age=7 tonight, budgets engage at next deploy). NOT done: (c) delta/ref-count materialization of near-identical consecutive snapshots — real but separate design work; worst-case steady state is now bounded at ~16 GiB/workspace so the pressure is off.
